name: AMC1300BDWVR
title: ±250 mV input, gain 8.2, reinforced isolated amplifier for shunt current sensing

source.revision: SBAS895D, May 2018, revised May 2022 (addendum pages dated 2026)

summary: The AMC1300 measures a small differential voltage, usually across a current shunt, on one side of a reinforced capacitive isolation barrier and reproduces it, multiplied by a fixed 8.2, as a differential voltage around 1.44 V on the other side. Inside, a delta-sigma modulator turns the input into a bitstream, the bitstream crosses the SiO2 barrier by on-off keying, and an analog filter rebuilds the signal. The barrier is rated 5000 VRMS for one minute (UL 1577) and 7071 VPK transient (VDE 0884-11). It flags a missing high-side supply or an input common-mode fault with a negative fail-safe output. The AMC1300B grade adds 3.3 V high-side operation, tighter offset and gain, and higher CMTI.

circuits.title: Shunt current sensing in a half-bridge (Figure 9-1)
circuits.description: The phase current of an inverter leg passes through RSHUNT between the switch node and the load. The high side of the AMC1300B floats on the switch node: GND1 and INN are tied to the shunt's switch-node end, and VDD1 is taken from the upper gate driver's floating supply through a series resistor, clamped by a zener and bypassed by 1 µF and 100 nF. Each input reaches the shunt through 10 Ω, with 10 nF across INP and INN as the input filter. The low side runs from a 3.3 V or 5 V supply bypassed by 1 µF and 100 nF, and its differential output drives the ADC through an RC filter.

circuits.title: Decoupling and input filter (Figure 10-1)
circuits.description: The basic hookup around the part. C1 (100 nF) and C2 (1 µF) bypass VDD1 to GND1, C3 (100 nF) and C4 (1 µF) bypass VDD2 to GND2. The shunt's upper end feeds INP through R2, its lower end feeds INN through R1, and C5 across the pins completes the input filter. GND1 is a separate connection to the shunt's lower end. OUTP and OUTN go on to an RC filter or ADC.

circuits.title: Differential to single-ended output stage (Figure 9-3)
circuits.description: A TLV6001 difference amplifier turns the differential output into one voltage about VREF for a single-ended ADC. OUTN reaches the inverting input through R1, with R2 and C1 in parallel as feedback; OUTP reaches the non-inverting input through R3, with R4 and C2 from that node to VREF. With all four resistors equal the gain is one and the output is (VOUTP – VOUTN) + VREF; C1 and C2 set the stage bandwidth. R1 to R4 are 3.3 kΩ and C1, C2 330 pF.

operation.text: Two grades come in the same DWV package. AMC1300B: VDD1 from 3.0 V, specified –55 °C to 125 °C, offset ±0.2 mV max, gain error ±0.3 % max, CMTI 100 kV/µs min, bandwidth 310 kHz typ. AMC1300: VDD1 from 4.5 V only, specified –40 °C to 125 °C, offset ±2 mV, gain error ±1 %, CMTI 15 kV/µs min, bandwidth 230 kHz typ.

A fully differential input amplifier, its gain fixed by on-chip precision resistors (differential input resistance RIND), drives a second-order switched-capacitor feed-forward delta-sigma modulator on the high side. The bitstream crosses a capacitive SiO2 barrier; on the low side a fourth-order analog filter rebuilds it into the differential voltage on OUTP and OUTN. The barrier is highly immune to magnetic fields.

Bits cross the barrier by on-off keying: a 480 MHz nominal carrier is sent for a one and nothing for a zero. The receiver demodulates it and feeds the output filter. The channel is tuned for high CMTI and low radiated emission from the carrier and buffer switching.

Outside the absolute-maximum input voltage range the ESD diodes conduct, and input current must then be held within the absolute maximum (±10 mA). Linearity and the specified performance hold only while the differential input stays in VFSR (±250 mV) and the common-mode voltage stays in the operating VCM range (–0.16 V to VDD1 – 2.1 V).

Linear response with gain 8.2 from –250 mV to +250 mV differential input. Between 250 mV and 320 mV the output keeps rising with poorer linearity. Beyond VClipping (±320 mV) the outputs saturate at VCLIPout (±2.49 V typ differential).

The output is driven to VFAILSAFE, a negative differential voltage (–2.57 V typ, –2.53 V max) that normal operation never produces, when VDD1 is absent or below VDD1UV (2.6 V typ, falling), or when the input common-mode voltage exceeds VCMov (VDD1 – 2 V, 60 mV hysteresis). The maximum VFAILSAFE, –2.53 V, is the threshold to compare against at system level.
The part runs whenever both VDD1 and VDD2 are within their recommended ranges; the supplies need no power-up order. After VDD1 steps to 3.0 V the outputs settle to 0.1 % within tAS, 500 µs typ.
Inputs must not float while powered: the input bias current can pull them positive past the operating common-mode range, and the part then outputs the fail-safe level.

GND1 comes from the INN end of the shunt, by a short or through a resistance; a DC path from INN to GND1 is required. For best offset and accuracy, run GND1 as its own trace to the shunt instead of joining it to INN at the device pins. With a four-terminal shunt, INP and INN take the inner (sense) leads and GND1 the INN-side outer lead. In the typical application VDD1 comes from the floating supply of the upper gate driver.

An RC filter ahead of the input improves SNR. Its corner should be at least ten times below the 20 MHz modulator sampling frequency, its DC resistance low enough that the bias current (–30 µA typ) drops little voltage across it, and the impedance seen from INP equal to that from INN. 10 Ω in each input with 10 nF across the pins (Figure 9-2) suits most designs.

For a single-ended ADC, a TLV6001 difference amplifier (Figure 9-3) gives (VOUTP – VOUTN) + VREF when R1 = R2 = R3 = R4. 3.3 kΩ resistors with 330 pF capacitors suit most applications; the stage bandwidth is set to what the system needs.
A short delay through the amplifier lets the system shut down quickly on overcurrent; Figure 9-4 shows the full-scale step response.

VDD1 takes a low-ESR 100 nF and a low-ESR 1 µF capacitor in parallel to GND1, and VDD2 the same pair to GND2, all four as close to the part as possible. MLCCs lose much of their nominal value under DC bias, low-profile ones most, so they are sized from capacitance-against-bias curves.

Place the decoupling capacitors right at the supply pins. Place the shunt close to INP and INN and keep the two input connections symmetrical. Keep the area under the package between the two sides clear of any conductive material (Figure 11-1).

The TDDB projection of the reinforced isolation capacitor, at up to 150 °C and 60 Hz, supports a 1500 VRMS working voltage for 135 years (operating zone) and holds 1800 VRMS for 254 years (safety-margin zone), on a line set at less than 1 ppm failure rate. The 20 % and 87.5 % marks set the margins between the zones.

The example land pattern gives 9.1 mm nominal clearance and creepage, with pads of (1.8) by (0.6) mm on a (1.27) mm pitch and (10.9) mm between pad rows. Non-solder-mask-defined pads have the mask opening 0.07 mm max larger all round; solder-mask-defined pads have the mask overlapping the metal by 0.07 mm min all round. The stencil example keeps the same apertures for a 0.125 mm stencil.
